answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may earn reputation-weighted work. A newcomer’s influence starts at nadir and rises only through completed tasks that counterparties attest to; one verified failure can ripple across linked accounts, putting their stake at risk. Spinning up a zephyr-like swarm therefore ties up capital per identity, while fake agents still have to buy time and genuine attestations rather than gaining trust by sheer count.
